config.title: AbortController & Cleanup in useEffect

intro.title: AbortController & Cleanup in useEffect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue component that fetches and displays user data from an API, learning how to prevent memory leaks and unnecessary network requests. You will use the AbortController interface to cancel ongoing fetch requests when the component is no longer needed. The core concept involves implementing cleanup logic within Vue's `onUnmounted` lifecycle hook, similar to the cleanup function in React's `useEffect`. This ensures your application remains efficient and responsive by properly handling asynchronous operations. You'll work with Vue 3's Composition API, JavaScript's fetch API, and reactive state to manage the data flow.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, AbortController is essential for managing asynchronous operations in dynamic interfaces like search bars, dashboards with live filters, and data tables. When users rapidly type in a search field or toggle between filter options, AbortController prevents outdated network requests from completing and potentially overwriting current results. This pattern ensures that data-intensive components like analytics dashboards or e-commerce product listings remain responsive and display only the most relevant information. Developers implement this cleanup logic to create smoother user experiences and reduce unnecessary server load.

objectives: Initialize an AbortController instance within a Vue component's setup function
Integrate the AbortController's signal into a fetch request to enable cancellation
Configure a cleanup function in onUnmounted to abort pending fetch requests
Apply the AbortController pattern to prevent memory leaks in asynchronous operations
Construct a reactive data property to store fetched data and handle loading states
Implement error handling for aborted requests using try-catch blocks
Manipulate component state to reflect cancellation and cleanup outcomes

steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue APIs for reactive state management.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'AbortControllerDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a component that exports an object with a setup function. The setup function should return an object (even if empty for now).

successCriteria: Component named 'AbortControllerDemo' exists with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure.

steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't set up correctly. Create a Vue component named 'AbortControllerDemo' with a setup function that returns an object.

steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive variable named 'data' using ref to store fetched data. Initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Use ref('') to create a reactive reference that will hold the data from your fetch request.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const message = ref('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive 'data' variable ready to store fetched content.
successCriteria: A reactive variable named 'data' is created using ref with an initial empty string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref('') to initialize the data variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reactive data variable wasn't created correctly. Try using ref('') inside the setup function.

steps.title: Initialize loading state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, initialize a reactive loading variable using ref, setting its initial value to false.
steps.hint: Use ref(false) to create a reactive loading state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: reactive loading state
const isLoading = ref(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive loading variable is created to track when data fetching is in progress.
successCriteria: The loading variable is declared with ref(false) inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref(false) to initialize the loading variable inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a reactive loading variable using ref(false) inside the setup function.

steps.title: Create fetchData function with AbortController
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named fetchData that instantiates an AbortController and uses it in a fetch request. The function should be async and accept no parameters.
steps.hint: Declare an async function fetchData() {}. Inside, create a new AbortController and use its signal property in a fetch call.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fetchData function is defined inside setup, ready to be called later. It includes an AbortController instance and uses its signal in a fetch request.
successCriteria: The fetchData function is declared as async, instantiates an AbortController, and includes a fetch call with the controller's signal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure fetchData is async, creates an AbortController, and uses its signal in the fetch options.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function is missing or incomplete. It should be an async function that creates an AbortController and uses it in fetch.

steps.title: Add cleanup function to fetchData
steps.instruction: Modify your fetchData function to return a cleanup function that calls abort() on the AbortController instance.
steps.hint: After creating the AbortController and starting the fetch, return a function that calls controller.abort().
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData function now returns a cleanup function that can abort the fetch request when called.
successCriteria: fetchData returns a function that calls controller.abort()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a function from fetchData that calls controller.abort().
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function should return a cleanup function that calls abort() on the AbortController.

steps.title: Add template structure with data display
steps.instruction: In the component's setup function, return a template object that conditionally renders loading, error, and data states.
steps.hint: Return an object with a template property that contains your HTML structure. Use Vue's template syntax with v-if or v-show for conditional rendering.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will return a template object that can conditionally display loading, error, and data states.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing conditional rendering for loading, error, and data display.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add fetch button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element to the template that calls the fetchData function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to attach the fetchData function as the click handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that triggers the fetchData function when clicked.
successCriteria: The template includes a button element with @click="fetchData".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it doesn't call fetchData when clicked. Make sure to use @click="fetchData".
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler. Add a button with @click="fetchData".

steps.title: Add cleanup button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a second button to your template that will abort the fetch request when clicked. Place it next to the existing fetch button and wire its click event to call the cleanup function.
steps.hint: You'll need to add another button element in the template with a @click handler. The handler should call the cleanup function that's returned from fetchData.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a cancel button in Vue template
<button @click="cancelRequest">Cancel Request</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have two buttons: one to fetch data and one to cancel the ongoing request. The cleanup button will be visible and functional.
successCriteria: A second button element is added to the template with @click="cleanup" or similar handler that calls the cleanup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it's properly wired to call the cleanup function. Check that the @click handler references the correct function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup button is missing or not properly connected. Remember to add a button element with @click="cleanup" or similar handler that calls the cleanup function.
